Here are the findings on the tempering issues.  Reviewing the tempering the chocolate was fairly steady when watching the unit 





I had Justin take a temperature of the chocolate going into the mini temper unit, it was 96 F degrees 

The buffer tank was set at 90 F but the real temperature was 96 F

That led me to investigate the melting tank and it was set at 60 C which is 140 F.  The real temperature was 132 F. “Adding chocolate to the tank will result in a lower actual temperature”

We changed this to 52 C which is 125 F.  This has been our setting in the past.

Basically when we started the buffer tank was around 90 degrees allowing the Mini Temper to work correctly.  

As we stated using up the chocolate in the buffer tank it pulled from the melting tank and that chocolate started getting hotter over time as the 132 F temp was added.  

The longer we ran the hotter it got in the buffer tank and the worse results we started getting at the mini temper unit.

What it looks like happened is we reprogrammed the system due to the automated pump process and changed to temperature to match closer to what the grid melter are. 

I’ll work with Erandy Garcilazo Ceja to create a training on grid melters vs tank melting and train the teams on the difference
